transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Lena Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen, Daniel Ortiz, Priya Singh, Alex Zhao (Northbridge)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC check-in focused on finalizing rollout and go-live plan. Discussed canary strategy, A/B traffic split, cutover checklist, monitoring and runbooks, security/KMS and audit logging needs, and next steps for a rehearsal cutover. Action items captured.

Topics:
- Canary + A/B split approach
- Cutover checklist & runbook (prewarm, KV cache, DNS, capacity)
- Monitoring, dashboards, alerts, SLOs
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts
- Dedicated capacity vs hosted fallback during ramp

Action items (captured separately in metadata)

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. This is our weekly POC sync for Northbridge, focus today is rollout and go-live. Quick roll-call?
[00:08] Maya: Hey all, Maya here.
[00:09] Daniel: Daniel, on platform.
[00:11] Priya: Priya from security.
[00:13] Alex: Alex, product.
[00:15] Ravi: Ravi, Redwood SE.
[00:17] Lena: Cool. Quick agenda, we want to nail the canary cadence, A/B plan, monitoring and cutover runbook, and confirm who's owning what for the rehearsal.

[00:30] Maya: Our timeline is still the same, we want to be able to cutover traffic by end of month, ideally a progressive rollout. POC metrics have been good but we need confidence about runbook ops and compliance.
[00:42] Lena: Great, thanks. Ravi, can you run through the canary approach you suggested last week?

[00:50] Ravi: Sure. So proposal: two-phase canary. Phase 1 is internal low-traffic canary — like 1% of non-critical traffic for 48 hours, that's to validate correctness and warm caches. Phase 2 is expanded canary (10-20%) with production traffic characteristics for 72 hours, monitor p50/p95 latency, error rate, and regen quality checks. We include a smoke test suite that runs every 15 minutes. If any threshold trip, immediate rollback to hosted endpoint or previous model.
[01:20] Daniel: Can you clarify the rollback mechanism, like is it DNS, routing policy, or a config flip? We want it to be quick and auditable.
[01:29] Ravi: It's an orchestration config flip inside Redwood's routing layer — we have an API that can shift traffic by percentage, and we keep the previous model pinned so rollback is immediate. We'll also provide a runbook step for DNS TTLs if customer-level DNS is involved.

[01:45] Priya: From security POV, we need to ensure keys and KMS are set and rotation tested before canary. Also audit logs for each switch are required for our compliance team. Do you have examples?
[01:57] Lena: Yes, we'll share sample audit logs and KMS config. Ravi, can you pull the SOC 2 / KMS notes?
[02:03] Ravi: Yep will add. Quick note — if you use Redwood Private in your VPC, keys can remain in your KMS, Redwood only gets encrypted blobs. If you're on Hosted we'll outline KMS integration options.

[02:20] Alex: For A/B we want to measure not just latency but perceived quality delta — a small set of golden prompts and some human evals. Also cost delta per 1k tokens so product can weigh economics.
[02:33] Lena: Agreed. We'll include a sample evaluation harness and spreadsheet. We'll recommend an initial 50/50 A/B for 24 hours on a representative slice, collect metrics, then decide.

[02:50] Maya: What about prewarming? We saw cold start p95 on a couple of flows during the POC.
[02:57] Ravi: Prewarming strategy: keep a small baseline pool of sessions active for critical routes, and a prefix KV cache warm-up run during the maintenance window. For Dedicated we can reserve capacity to avoid cold starts; on Hosted there's a small warm-up job that can be scheduled. Note: KV cache warm-up is incremental — initial tokens will be heavier.

[03:20] Daniel: Can you quantify the capacity we need to reserve to hit our p95 target?
[03:25] Ravi: Based on POC traffic mix, to get p95 under 600ms for 2k-3k qps on our model we recommend a 20% buffer above baseline. We'll send detailed numbers in the runbook. There's a tradeoff with cost; we can do dynamic scaling with a short autoscale window but that can increase transient latencies.

[03:46] Alex: So during canary do we prefer reserved Dedicated nodes or Hosted with fallback to Dedicated?
[03:53] Lena: For rollout we recommend reserved Dedicated for primary, with Hosted as a fallback if Dedicated has capacity constraints. That gives predictable throughput and isolation. But for cost, many customers start on Hosted and move to Dedicated as they ramp.

[04:10] Priya: If we use Dedicated, the requirement is that all logs are forwarded to our Splunk and that KMS rotation meets our policy. Also we need proof of encryption in transit and at rest.
[04:21] Ravi: We'll share a short doc + examples of audit exports — includes S3 bucket names for log exports, sample event formats.

[04:30] Maya: Monitoring — what dashboard and alerts should we have for the canary? We want to avoid alert fatigue but catch regressions quickly.

[04:38] Daniel: Suggested signals: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, token cost per response, user-facing error rate, KL divergence or other quality metric on golden set, and model fallback counts. A composite health score would be nice.

[04:54] Ravi: We'll provide a Grafana template: panels for latency (p50/p95), errors, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and a quality panel with golden prompt results. Alerts: p95 > target for 5 consecutive minutes, error rate > 0.5% sustained, quality delta worse than threshold.

[05:15] Alex: For A/B evaluation we want automated collection of golden prompt responses and an initial human-in-the-loop sample of 100 responses per variant. Who's owning the eval?
[05:24] Maya: Northbridge will do the initial human evals; Redwood to publish the harness and golden prompt set.

[05:30] Ravi: We'll also add automatic failure annotations where an automated check fails to help triage.

[05:38] Daniel: Cutover rehearsal — suggestion: a dry-run where we do config flips without traffic and then a scheduled low-traffic canary. Can we do the dry-run 11/18 and canary 11/19?
[05:48] Lena: That works on Redwood side. Maya, does that fit your ops calendar?
[05:51] Maya: Yes, 11/18 for rehearsal, 11/19 for canary window is good.

[06:00] Priya: Security wants a checklist for the rehearsal: KMS keys rotated, audit logging enabled, RBAC validated, incident contact list confirmed.
[06:08] Lena: We'll bake that into the runbook checklist.

[06:13] Ravi: One more point on rollback automation — we can wire the canary to an automatic rollback which triggers after two alert thresholds. But we recommend manual confirmation for the first 24 hours to avoid flip-flopping on noisy signals.

[06:28] Alex: What about data retention — for logs and prompts we need retention policy for regulatory reasons.
[06:34] Priya: We need 7 years for some dataset subsets but most logs can be 1 year. We'll provide specifics.

[06:42] Lena: Noted. We'll include retention configuration options in the runbook and log export examples.

[06:50] Maya: Anything about model variants? We have internal smaller model for cheap inference — prefer fallbacks to a cheaper variant if high load rather than dropping requests.

[06:59] Ravi: Yes, Redwood routing supports model variants and fallback policies. Policy example: if latency spikes, route 30% of non-critical traffic to smaller model for 2 hours and monitor quality on golden set. We'll document recommended policies.

[07:15] Daniel: Is there a cost estimate for the fallback strategy? We need to show finance the delta.
[07:20] Lena: We'll include cost scenarios in the pricing note — expected cost per 100k tokens under normal, vs dedicated reserved, vs fallback.

[07:29] Maya: For the rehearsal, who is the single point contact on Redwood side?
[07:33] Lena: I'll be the AE owner for scheduling and comms, Ravi will be the technical runbook lead during the rehearsal.

[07:40] Priya: For compliance we might need a short non-prod to prod signing checklist.

[07:44] Lena: We'll add that, and include who signs off — likely Priya and Maya for policy, Daniel for platform.

[07:52] Alex: Anything else on metrics? We want to capture latency tail, cost, quality, and user-facing errors. Also capture per-route metrics.

[07:59] Ravi: We'll provide a per-route dashboard and routing traces so you can see which route a request took and KV cache hit rates.

[08:10] Maya: One more ask — can we get sample runbook with timing estimates for each step, e.g., prewarm 30 mins, verify health 10 mins, shift 10% every hour, etc.

[08:20] Lena: Yes, we'll include a step-by-step cutover checklist with estimated times and who owns each step.

[08:30] Daniel: Great, thanks. Next steps recap?

[08:33] Lena: I'll share the runbook draft by Friday (2025-11-14). Ravi will prepare canary configs and Grafana template. Daniel to provision dashboards and grant access. Priya to list security signoffs. Alex to finalize A/B success criteria. We'll do dry-run 11/18 and canary 11/19.

[08:55] Maya: Sounds good.
[08:57] Lena: Any blockers?
[08:59] Priya: Not yet, just need the docs for legal review.
[09:02] Daniel: We'll get infra ready by 11/15.
[09:05] Lena: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread with the runbook link and calendar invites for the rehearsal and canary.

[09:15] Alex: Thanks all.
[09:17] Meeting end.

References / artifacts mentioned:
- Runbook draft (link to be shared): https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/northbridge-cutover-draft
- Grafana template: https://redwood.example.com/monitoring/templates/northbridge-grafana.json
- Pricing & capacity spreadsheet (internal link)
- SOC2/KMS sample logs: will be shared via secure share

Final recap (verbatim):
"Run rehearsal 11/18 (dry-run), canary 11/19 (1% then 10-20%), monitoring thresholds p95 and error rate, manual confirmation for first 24 hrs, rollback automation enabled but manual for day 1, provide runbook by 11/14."

End of transcript.
